36.0.0.en: The Gileadites: the sons of Gilead the son of Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh the son of Joseph; that is, they were one of the clans of the tribe of Manasseh.

36.0.1.en: The heads of the clan of the Gileadites came to Moses to present a problem concerning their tribe and its portion in the land, relating to one of their brethren named Zelophehad, who had died and had no son to inherit the land, but had five daughters. The heads began their speech to Moses by reminding him of what the Lord had commanded earlier (ch. 27), that the daughters of Zelophehad must inherit their father's portion of the land.

36.1.0.en: The plea and complaint that the men raised was that if these daughters married men from other tribes of the people, their lands would be joined to the possessions of their husbands, and therefore to the other tribes; and because this land was an inheritance and not a sale or purchase, the tribe of Manasseh would not be able to recover it in the year of Jubilee (which is the fiftieth year, in which, as the Law established, purchased lands return to their original owners). Naturally, if this happened, the land of the tribe of Manasseh would decrease and the lands of the other tribes, those of the husbands, would increase, and this is contrary to what the Lord commanded, that each tribe keep its portion without diminution.

36.1.1.en: The following is evident from the way the heads of the Gileadites presented the problem to Moses:

36.1.2.en: 1- Their concern to study the Law and apply it in their lives.

36.1.3.en: 2- Their claiming of their rights, for this shows their concern for their inheritance and for God's gift to them.

36.1.4.en: Be careful to keep your inheritance from God, which is your portion in the Church of the Holy Sacraments, and your concern for your eternal inheritance, so that you live in repentance and cleaving to God through prayers and readings, and Satan does not steal your portion and take you with him to eternal torment.

36.2.s.en: (2) God's answer to the complaint of the heads

36.2.0.en: God's answer to Moses was that what the heads of the Gileadites, of the tribe of Manasseh, had spoken was right, and represented zeal for their land and for the Law that God had set down.

36.3.0.en: God's command on this matter was as follows: since the daughters of Zelophehad would inherit their father's land, they were to marry whom they wished among the men, but only from within the clan and the tribe, so that the land and the portions would not be mixed among the tribes, and thus each tribe would hold fast and cleave ("keep") to its land and not sacrifice the portion of its fathers.

36.4.0.en: From the problem of the daughters of Zelophehad, God lays down a general law for all the children of Israel: every girl who inherits from her father must marry one of the sons of the same clan and tribe, so that the inheritance of the fathers is not dissipated and mixed among the tribes, but each tribe remains in possession of the first allotment that God determined for it.

36.4.1.en: Note: it is understood from the text, the context, and the later Jewish tradition that God did not forbid the inheriting daughters from marrying outside their tribes, but in that case her right to inherit the land is forfeited and nothing is added to her husband (ch. 27:9-11).

36.5.0.en: The daughters of Zelophehad adhered to what the Lord commanded, and indeed married their cousins, and therefore kept their portion of the land.

36.5.1.en: What the heads presented to Moses was not wrong; rather, it can be regarded as vigilance and care for the Law and for the tribe's portion of the land of the fathers that God had given them, especially since they presented their problem to Moses, the man of God, His representative and the leader of his people. Likewise, there is no objection to our presenting our problems to God and to the Church, and through prayer God will answer our questions through His voice within us or through the opinion of the Church, and this is far better than lawsuits and courts, which rob a person of his peace and his love for others.

36.6.0.en: With this verse the Book of Numbers is concluded, making clear that, before the crossing and the entry into Canaan, while they were still east of the Jordan in the plains of Moab, the Lord gave His people these closing commandments, which began from (ch. 26) and extend to the problem of the daughters of Zelophehad. They included the command for the final census of the people, the division of the land, the cities of refuge, laws concerning the Levites, laws concerning vows, the command to fight the Midianites and to defeat them, and to shun pagan worship completely... Thus ended the book that recorded the journey of the people from their departure from the land of Egypt, throughout forty years, up to just before their entry into the Promised Land.
